extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, industry partners, national laboratories, state/local governments, and nongovernment organizations interested in applying for Solar Energy Technologies Office (SETO) funding/NOFOs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and programmatic priorities for proposing projects to the U.S. Department of Energy Solar Energy Technologies Office (SETO), including how Notices of Funding Opportunity (NOFOs) are developed, evaluated, and negotiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: SETO program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: to improve the affordability, reliability, and security of solar energy on the electric grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align with the office’s overall goals to improve affordability, reliability, and security of solar on the grid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drive innovation and American-made affordability/supply-chain security
rubrics_metrics.description: Drive innovation to make American-made solar technology affordable and its supply chain secure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SETO funds R&D that advances innovation and reduces costs while strengthening domestic manufacturing and supply-chain security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable solar with storage for grid reliability/resilience/security
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable solar energy with storage to support the reliability, resilience, and security of the electricity grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that integrate storage to improve grid reliability, resilience, or security are priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide relevant, objective technical information to cut red tape
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide relevant and objective technical information to cut red tape and meet growing electricity demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SETO places value on producing technical outputs that reduce regulatory or procedural barriers and support electricity demand growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOFO development through collaborative process
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) ... is developed through a collaborative process in order to achieve the office's goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFOs are shaped collaboratively to ensure alignment with SETO goals; applicants should read NOFOs for explicitly stated priorities and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, highly competitive solicitation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhering to an open, highly competitive solicitation process, these funding opportunities encourage collaborative partnerships among industries; universities; national laboratories; federal, state, and local governments; and nongovernment organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect competitive review; proposals that demonstrate strong collaborations across sectors are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged collaborative partnerships (eligible/target participants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage collaborative partnerships among industries; universities; national laboratories; federal, state, and local governments; and nongovernment organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortia or multi-party collaborations spanning these types of organizations are favored by the office’s solicitation approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous peer review of NOFO applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NOFO applications undergo a rigorous peer review process before projects are selected for negotiation to receive DOE funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals will be evaluated through peer review; applicants should prepare clear, well-justified technical and programmatic rationales to withstand rigorous evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-selection negotiation and collaborative project planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the successful completion of this negotiation process, including collaboration on a statement of project objectives, milestones, and budgets, projects can begin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected applicants should be prepared to negotiate and collaboratively finalize project objectives, milestones, and budgets prior to award execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for cooperative research and development projects in targeted research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: SETO funds cooperative research and development projects in several research areas that drive innovation and lower costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose R&D that targets SETO-identified research areas and demonstrates potential to lower costs and drive innovation; review NOFO text for specific research area definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prizes and challenges to accelerate innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: SETO also funds prizes and challenges to encourage innovation and accelerate the development of new solar energy solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to traditional grants/agreements, SETO uses prize competitions and challenges — applicants should monitor office announcements for such opportunities and design proposals/teams appropriate to prize formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on specific, measurable results
rubrics_metrics.description: Success stories help to show the specific, measurable results from these projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded projects are expected to deliver tangible, measurable outcomes (e.g., cost reductions, technology performance improvements); proposals should include clear metrics and milestones to demonstrate impact.
